observations: Private-rationale staleness (non-blocking, conservative direction): rationale items (3) and CONTROL HISTORY state that hmm-reformat-valid was the one unmet control and predict the grader rejects the probe's two-trailing-backslash STATS line. The freshly executed records for this candidate are authoritative and show that control passing (control_summary 22/22, probe_valid_execution true, submission mutated from 0253d73e... to 93d8d381..., all seven checks passed). The history quote is accurate against the author-supplied earlier summary (author_input_control_summary, 21/22), and revising the shipped grader was not required; no acceptance outcome rests on this description. Future records should cite the current 22/22 state.

Provenance nuance on 'independent programs': the oracle, the recomputed control and the independently executed solve.py all use pyhmmer 0.12.3 (HMMER 3.4 C engine), so they are independent wrappers rather than independent algorithmic implementations. The tolerance basis primarily rests on serialization precision (4-5 decimals on HMM parameters, one decimal on scores, two significant digits on E-values, two decimals on accuracy), which is sound and sufficient; cross-engine independence is neither claimed nor needed, and the tolerance-boundaries probe (x1.05 E-values, +0.06 scores, +0.006 accuracy, +0.0012 HMM values all failing) confirms the boundaries in both directions.

Minor wording precision, resolved by the full contract: the one-line check description for domtbl_domain_rows_match says 'and vice versa' while the code anchors the pair comparison on the reference pair set and delegates submission-only targets to check 5's exact target-set equality; the grader addendum (check 6) documents the anchoring explicitly and the executed controls (domtbl-extra-target-added fails 5 with 4/6/7 passing; domtbl-domain-multiplicity-extra fails 6's extra-pair and 'of' comparisons) confirm the documented behavior, so the combined public contract is unambiguous.

Domtbl E-value relative tolerance uses max(|submitted|,|reference|) as denominator; the x1.05 boundary probe exceeds 0.02 under either denominator interpretation, so the residual ambiguity is immaterial for the accepted/rejected boundaries observed.

The HMM continuation latitude (single or trailing doubled backslash joining, doubled backslash consumed as the continuation marker, documented in the addendum) only affects how physical lines join; all numeric/identity comparisons still run at full rigor on the joined content, so the latitude cannot accept changed probabilities, and the valid-alternative control (respelled numerics, split STATS line, no DATE/COM) exercises it as intended.
rationale: The revised candidate is suitable for packaging. Public contract and code agree on all seven checks; all 22 freshly executed controls (reference, empty, misplaced, 2 missing, recomputed, alternative, 15 probes = 2 valid alternatives + 13 wrong-solutions) meet their intended outcomes. Path semantics verified from submission hash records (root-relative keys; the misplaced control with outputs/-prefixed keys fails as documented). Source coverage is complete: both terminal scientific artifacts (LuxC.hmm, LuxC.domtbl) are compared at full rigor — header identities (NAME, alphabet/order, LENG vs body node count, NSEQ, CKSUM), every emission/transition value position-aligned with '*' zero semantics, and complete domtbl record coverage and multiplicity (target-set equality in check 5 plus reference-anchored (target, domain) pair coverage with extra-domain rejection in check 6). Tolerances (1e-3 abs HMM, 0.05 abs scores/biases, 0.02 rel E-values, 0.005 abs accuracy) have a defensible serialization-precision basis and are confirmed in both directions by the recomputed/alternative runs and the just-past-tolerance boundary probe. Meaningful wrong outputs (wrong calibrations, shifted emissions, '*' replacement, extra insert value, wrong Z/domZ search spaces, swapped attributes, extra targets/domains, block-order violations, nonfinite/out-of-range values, query-name mismatch) all fail through check comparisons rather than crashes or malformed files. The two grader-side repairs are validated: check-6 wording now matches the code's reference-anchored comparison (recorded controls confirm the documented division of labor with check 5), and nonfinite nan/inf/± spellings in the HMM model body are now explicitly rejected as invalid values without changing any acceptance outcome. The previously unmet hmm-reformat-valid control now passes on fresh execution of the unchanged probe script, and its passing is consistent with the current grader's publicly documented continuation-joining rules. No answer leakage (all expected values read from the reference at grading time), no hardcoded result shapes, no control-name detection, and no acceptance-rule weakening was needed.

source_coverage.rationale: Audited against the converted source (inputs/original.py, exports.py), the preparation plan (inputs/plan.json) and the export code. The source's two terminal written scientific products - the profile HMM saved from builder.build_msa (LuxC.hmm) and the domain hits table from pipeline.search_hmm (LuxC.domtbl) - are both independently evaluated by the grader at full content depth. The two excluded outputs are diagnostic with source-backed reasons: hmm.consensus is an in-notebook inspection ('We can have a look at the consensus sequence') whose content is contained in the saved HMM (per-node CONS/match emissions that are compared), and the printed first-hit alignment (print(ali)) is a demonstrative display of TopHits access whose quantitative content (coordinates, envelope, scores, E-values, accuracy) is covered by the domtbl row comparisons and was never serialized as an artifact in the source. No additional eligible terminal result exists in the original script; no preparation-inventory omission or scientific scope change was found. The scientific question (build and search) is preserved as a single task with no excluded eligible branches.
